correctness.rationale: Every derivation is uniquely encoded by (a,b) in k[s]/(s^m); original square/commutator equations reduce exactly to ab=b²=0 and a_i b_j+a_j b_i=0. Minimal valuation forces all tuple entries into a common L_j, with converse by multiplication. Direct affine-linear dimensions, intersections and nested neighbor inclusion-exclusion establish the component arrangement. Ranks follow from multiplication by (a,b); finite field submodule counts produce every joint rank coefficient. Independent direct-matrix computations over F2, F4, F8 confirm original identities and sample joint histograms. Boundary m=1 and parity N=2m/2m+1 explicitly accounted for. No assertion about nonreduced schemes.

value.rationale: Complete multivariate rank spectra of commuting square-zero tuples are intrinsic and motivated by elementary-abelian restricted Lie representations; they quantify correlations unavailable from the prior one-operator nullcone census. This work supplies a simultaneous common-component rigidity theorem, all irreducible component/intersection dimensions and exact every-arity rank polynomials uniformly in finite fields and truncation degrees, with parity stability. No arbitrary cutoff, parameter-only gain, or known-table recomputation is relied upon. Potential use is in counting restricted nilpotent representations with fixed operator ranks; no downstream theorem is asserted as proved.
